problem: A cyclist accelerates with constant acceleration from $0\,\text{m/s}$ to $20\,\text{m/s}$ in $10$ seconds. Find their acceleration.

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/352f3d049bd57a805419a34a7873f37f30c95cb2c7c28f4cac984584ff646c75.png)

The speed-time graph represents the motion of a bus. Calculate the acceleration of the bus.
feedback.worked_solution:
In a speed-time graph, the acceleration is given by the slope of the line.

The line passes through the points $(0,0)$ and $(4,2),$ so its slope is:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{2\,\text{m/s}-0\,\text{m/s}}{4\,\text{s}-0\,\text{s}} \\  & =\frac{2\,\text{m/s}}{4\,\text{s}} \\  & =0.5\,\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration of the bus is $0.5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
